COLLEGE MUSIC SYMPOSIUM
The
College Music Symposium
is a CMS unit entailing a scholarly journal and an affiliated digital resource repository.
General Editor:
Lisa Urkevich
,
This email address is being protected from spambots. You need JavaScript enabled to view it.
Editors:
James A. Grymes
,
Jacquelyn Sholes
,
Josef Hanson
,
Thomas Kurtz
,
Daniel Walzer
,
Julian Bennett Holmes
,
Mark Nowakowski
Editorial Board
Aim and Scope
The
College Music Symposium: Journal of the College Music Society
is a double-blind peer-reviewed journal that publishes research, comprehensive review articles, forums, and individual reviews, including those of books, audio, technologies, and online platforms. The journal also publishes, with transcriptions, peer-reviewed Performances, Lectures, Lecture-Recitals, and Lessons (PLL) that have been captured on video.
Symposium
issues are officially released twice a year Summer/Fall and Winter/Spring.
The
College Music Symposium,
which was first published in 1961, was established with a unique purpose not duplicated elsewhere: it was a “different sort of scholarly journal,” a provocative publication that “cuts across lines of specialization...into the liberal arts college or the professional music school,” serving an impressive array of professionals, including the music scholar, performer, composer, educator, and administrator. (McCorkle
Symposium
1961). The present journal enhances the comprehensive vision by remaining fluid and addressing the dynamic interests and concerns of music professionals and educators into the 21st century.
ISSN: 00695696
EISSN: 2334203X
The
College Music Symposium
is indexed in major databases:
Scopus
JSTOR
RILM
EBSCO Discovery Service
Ex Libris - Primo Central
OCLC - WorldCat Discovery Service
Serials Solutions (ProQuest) - Summon
TDNet - TDNet Discover

History Of CMS
The College Music Society is dedicated to the advancement of music teaching, learning, scholarship, performance, and creative activity. Rooted in higher education, CMS serves as an inclusive forum for dialogue and collaboration among music professionals across all disciplines and career paths. We support faculty, students, independent scholars, and industry partners by fostering innovation, promoting diversity, and encouraging the exchange of ideas to shape the future of music in society. Through advocacy, professional development, and community engagement, CMS empowers its members to lead and inspire in academic, artistic, and entrepreneurial contexts.
312 East Pine Street | Missoula MT 59802 | USA
Ph: 406.721.9616 | Email:
[email protected]
| Web:
www.music.org

Sixty-Ninth National Conference (2026)
November 12 - November 14, 2026
Amway Grand Plaza
Grand Rapids, Michigan
Source: Iceportal Content
Adaptive Advocacy: Collegiate Music Training at a Crossroads
Dear CMS Members,
The 2026 CMS Program Committee is excited to announce calls for participation in the 69th CMS National Conference held at the Grand Rapids Amway Grand Plaza hotel in Grand Rapids, MI, from November 12 - 14, 2026. The conference will be held in conjunction with the Association for Technology in Music Instruction (ATMI), National Association for Collegiate Wind and Percussion Instructors (NACWPI), and Pi Kappa Lambda (PKL). On behalf of the
2026 CMS National Conference Program Committee
, I invite you to submit a proposal for participation.
The 2026 CMS National Conference Theme:
Adaptive Advocacy: Collegiate Music Training at a Crossroads
The world of collegiate music education is at a crossroads. Institutions of higher education face an array of challenges across technological, political, social, and economic paradigms, wherein creatives are poised to, together, imagine new models for sustainable music-making. The present moment asks each of us to envision what a vibrant future of music education, creation, performance, and scholarship might look like, in conversation with community-based action, coalition-building, advocacy, and innovative practice across all those realms. In line with the
2024-2025 Common Topic
, we invite submissions that highlight current creative work in the following areas:
Performances and lecture recitals that imagine new ways of understanding the music of the past and the present, with forward-thinking considerations on music-making in the coming decade
Professional activities that illustrate the capacity for artistic expression to intersect with social action through collaboration and coalition-building
Creative research projects that explore innovations in the field of music education, performance, scholarship, and composition, through the lens of advocacy and social justice
Explorations of emergent technologies that pose both opportunities and potential challenges to music-makers and educators
The Program Committee invites participation from across all music disciplines, both those affiliated with performing arts institutions and companies and independent scholars, composers, performers, and educators. This year, the Committee is also excited to announce two special initiatives. For the first time, the 2026 conference will include a special call for student poster submissions, as well as featured presentations by CMS Regional Chapter Student Award recipients. More information about all proposal submission formats, as well as the full conference description, can be found by clicking on the
“Calls for Program Participation”
link. All proposals are due no later than
11:59pm Mountain Time on Monday, January 5, 2026.
Please join us in Grand Rapids, Michigan, a vibrant community filled with opportunities to engage with culture, art-making, stunning natural beauty, a world-class local craft food and beverage scene, and, of course, music. Situated in the heart of the Midwest, it is the perfect place to come together, share, learn from one another, and imagine the potentialities of this crossroads moment. We can’t wait to see you there!
Sincerely,
Jonathan Kuuskoski
2026 CMS National Conference Program Committee Chair
